boundary.resolution: Sections 1 and 2 describe the two reading circuits, output control, local-memory input, and timing control. The opening figure separates their paths.

registers.resolution: Section 4 lists all 26 words, addresses, access rules, reset values, and decoded bit positions. Section 2.5 completes MMOD, AMOD, SLBG, and ALP operations. Unnamed retained bits are not must-zero bits.

datapath.resolution: Sections 2.1–2.5 specify geometry, interlace, two-byte local-memory words, packing, address equations and wrap, zero samples, composition order, RGB rounding and coefficient saturation, and separate alpha selection. Matching TS/C++ software is authoritative by explicit user decision; the independently fixed WebGPU discrepancy is recorded in pcrtc-webgpu-constant-blend.md. Section6 supplies exact bounded integer-quotient source selection with named signal/output/source units, nonzero first-sample phase and unequal step/magnification; both actual software consumers agree. Section7 isolates constant ALP versus doubled/saturated sample-alpha RGB coefficient and independent result alpha with four complete PMODE words; exact actual raw-RGBA replay corroborates all output rows separately from opaque PNGs.

visibility.resolution: Section 2.6 separates immediate programmed-word readback, the 22-word latch on VBlank entry before the system VBlank IRQ request, immediate beam restart on changed timing writes, and reset visibility. Separate writes can straddle the latch. The complete source/window program distinguishes programmed-word snapshots, fresh-after-write VBlank callback changes and separately captured output; no atomic multiword or universal timing guarantee is inferred.

timing.resolution: Section1.1 consolidates installed CPU/system frequency,13.5MHz beam reference, reset-derived microsecond/millisecond and rounded cycle deadlines, fractional phase and scalar/word-sequence CPU costs. Section2.7 retains exact timing equations/run conditions/FIELD/restart hazards. Undefined electrical clocks, pin widths, arbitration and sustained rates are explicitly not inferred.

interrupts.resolution: Sections 2.8 and 3.2 and the CSR/IMR entries cover HSINT/VSINT producers, the three retained event positions without normal producers, pending state, masks, acknowledgement, IRQ delivery, and the unmask race.

faults.resolution: Sections 2.10–2.11 establish ordinary CPU mapped-access widths, alignment, CPU modes, successive-word access, ignored high-word writes, synchronous exception causes, and the separate system bus fault latch. Pixel selectors and framebuffer wrap are deterministic, not format/address exceptions.

reset.resolution: Section 2.9 and CSR document action precedence, queued-input discard, retained-work retirement, readback cancellation, assembly-consumed partial-upload prefixes, reset versus flush scope, and the absence of local-memory clear/undo.

programming.resolution: Section 3 supplies ordered raw-word source/window and mask/acknowledge/unmask examples with explicit starting assumptions, derived values, latch visibility, output alpha, and the HSINT race. Hardware cautions are bounded by the sourced contracts. Section5 now supplies a complete154-line BLua/BIOS cartridge, exact raw stage words and source probes, and three actual output plates isolating source-origin versus output-window movement. Ordinary guest, independent source/image and byte-exact fresh-reader checks pass within the controlled ownership scope. Section6 adds a complete91-line executed BLua cartridge and actual8×1 output strip, all-source-word guest assertions, exact RGB checks and byte-exact fresh public-only reconstruction. Section7 supplies a complete125-line BLua cartridge and three real RGB plates from four phases, unchanged source/window/background state, raw source probes and fresh VBlank observations; A/B, B/C and B/D isolate MMOD, SLBG and AMOD respectively.
